_comment: Where tools/title_progress.py finds Test Drive Unlimited and what cannot be read from its sources. Paths are this machine's checkouts; nothing of the title is in this repository.
name: Test Drive Unlimited

sys.where: all eight groups, opt-in on `master`: `--any360_sys_groups=stateless,files,objects,threads,memory,xam,input,audio`; checked from boot through the intro videos, the title screen, a save loaded and the house menu to driving on the island (`--any360_sys_trace=true`, 2026-11-27): two calls still reach the runtime there, `XamEnumerate` and `NtClose` on the null handle `XamUserCreateStatsEnumerator` leaves; sound and rumble still to check by ear and hand

gfx.where: opt-in on `master`: `--any360_gpu=true` (`--any360_gpu_scale=2 --any360_gpu_msaa=4`; `--any360_gpu_vblank_hz=1000` lifts the 30 FPS lock); uncapped, driving at scale 1 on an RTX 5070 Ti: 115 FPS (1% low 101), 3.3 GB private, against 72 FPS (1% low 34) and 17-19 GB growing for the runtime's GPU (2026-11-27, 5 launches each)
todo: A rare resolve into a format the renderer refuses (host format 37 to guest format 4).
`any360_gpu_fences_after_draws=false` is faster but breaks this title's display: find what it waits on.

next: Give `XamUserCreateStatsEnumerator` a real enumerator (or the title's error path) so `XamEnumerate` and `NtClose` stop reaching the runtime with a null handle; then check sound, the gamepad's rumble and a long session in game.

Name what is left of the executable's library code: the ranges listed as not named in Any360's titles/tdu/modules.json (code shared with the other titles of unknown purpose, an XML parser, zlib, a JPEG path), then the game's own modules (Eden's ed* libraries carry their names in their strings).

More native replacements of library functions (the CRT's string routines next), each under the rule of Any360's docs/NATIVE_FUNCTIONS.md: a reference model, unit tests, a benchmark, then `--any360_xdk_verify=true` and `--any360_xdk_bench=true` in game.
A golden test target (guest sandbox) so rewritten game functions can be verified.
open: A game thread spins at 90% of a core (`sub_826737B8`).
Frame captures only trigger with `--any360_gpu_vblank_hz=1000` (the command processor is never idle at a kick otherwise).
The intro videos once ran too fast above 60 Hz; not seen again since the video pacing fix.
With `--any360_gpu_vblank_hz=1000` the vertical blanks arrive about every 2 ms: the menus stop at 240 FPS (the runtime's GPU, `--vsync=false`, reaches 500); driving runs far below it.
The runtime's GPU (`--any360_gpu=false`) uncapped grows by ~4 GB of private memory a minute (18 GB after 4 minutes); Any360's GPU stays flat.
